reason: The report estimates a causal effect from a bivariate regression with no controls, even though the data include pre-period confounders (productivity_2020, firm size, age, R&D, exports, credit score and others). Firms that were already more productive or better resourced plausibly choose more training, so the 2.29 coefficient is likely biased upward. Trimming the outcome adds an arbitrary sample restriction. I could not re-run the analysis, so I have no adjusted estimate to compare against.
